strengths: First large-scale spatial multigraph dataset filling a genuine gap in graph learning benchmarks; addresses the critical problem of multi-edge and geometric information loss in existing datasets
Exceptional scale (11.6M static + 5.1M dynamic graphs) and diversity (1401 classes) exceeding all existing simple graph datasets in class diversity

Significant technical contribution: Poly2Graph achieves 10^6× speedup and 20-40× memory efficiency through intelligent engineering (Frobenius matrices, adaptive resolution, GPU acceleration) with open-source MIT release
Comprehensive documentation with extensive mathematical background, algorithmic details, practical tutorials, and multiple dataset variants for different research needs
Physics-grounded approach using non-Hermitian band theory provides substantive motivation beyond artificial benchmark design
Principled representation of continuous edge geometry as ordered coordinate sequences, distinct from weighted edge aggregation approaches
Rigorous mathematical framework with validation through exact diagonalization comparisons
weaknesses: Critically incomplete benchmarking: Three largest datasets (HSG-three-band 9.1M, HSG-12M 11.6M, T-HSG-5M temporal) are completely unbenchmarked due to 'limited resources,' preventing verification that methods scale to intended dataset sizes or dataset utility at full scale

Poor baseline performance (Top-1 accuracy 46-69%) without diagnostic analysis: paper frames as 'headroom for improvement' but provides no explanation of what makes the task hard, no error analysis, and no proposed solutions or geometry-aware methods

Unclear practical motivation for graph-level classification by characteristic polynomial class; no demonstrated connection to applications in materials discovery, exotic phase discovery, or other real-world quantum physics problems

Component fragmentation limitation unresolved: Poly2Graph fails for high-band and long-range hopping systems precisely where method should be most useful; acknowledged but not addressed with solutions or systematic analysis

Arbitrary featurization choices (5 equidistant points, 13D edge features) without ablation studies or justification; no analysis of whether multi-edge structure is necessary versus weighted edges or alternative representations

Minimal analysis and diagnostic capability: missing graph property distributions, no error analysis correlating difficulty to structural properties, no exploration of extreme class imbalance (660:1 ratio in HSG-topology), limited exploration of why baselines fail
Incomplete temporal dataset contribution: T-HSG-5M introduced (5.1M graphs) but never benchmarked; no temporal models or guidance provided despite significant portion of contribution
Reproducibility concerns: 177 TB raw spectral data inaccessible; dataset generation details insufficient for reproducible extension; restricted 'limited resources' benchmarking limits verification

strengths: Large-scale, novel dataset of 11.6M spatial multigraphs addressing a documented gap in benchmarks
Technically well-engineered Poly2Graph pipeline with 10^6× speedup and thoughtful adaptive resolution strategy
Physics-grounded data source from non-Hermitian quantum physics provides intrinsic novelty and interest
Comprehensive documentation with mathematical background, detailed algorithms, and tutorials supporting reproducibility
Multiple dataset variants (HSG-one-band through HSG-12M) tailored to different research needs
Open-source release under permissive licenses with full code and data availability
weaknesses: Severely insufficient benchmarking: only 3 subsets evaluated (not full dataset), 4 standard models, weak results (Top-1 acc 14-53%), no ablation studies, no geometry-aware methods tested, no custom multigraph methods

Component fragmentation (failure on high-band systems) inadequately characterized—HSG-topology shows 660× class imbalance suggesting many affected graphs, with no systematic analysis of fraction affected or proposed solutions
Weak motivation for learning representations: why predict characteristic polynomial classes? No demonstrated scientific applications, physics benefits mentioned but never shown

Claimed 'new challenges for GNNs' not rigorously identified—no systematic characterization of what makes data difficult (edge multiplicity vs. geometry?), no analysis of which graph properties correlate with task difficulty
Incomplete dataset analysis: no data quality report, no distribution analysis, no outlier detection, no representation visualization, no feature importance analysis
Arbitrary featurization (5 equidistant edge points) without justification or ablation; paper acknowledges 'no agreed-upon standard' then proposes one without validation
Dataset construction appears arbitrary: why 13×7 coefficient sampling? Why −10−5i to 10+5i range? All intra-class graphs share topology—artificial similarity not analyzed

GNN experimental setup lacks rigor: fixed 5 epochs without early stopping, no justification for sum pooling, GraphSAGE dominates suggesting data properties not well-suited to expressive models, pattern unexplored
Temporal dataset (T-HSG-5M) under-utilized with no temporal benchmarks despite having temporal sequences
Overstated claims: 'universal relevance' via Toeplitz decomposition mathematically correct but non-unique, practical utility undemonstrated, feels like afterthought
Missing applications: no demonstration of value to condensed matter physics, no transfer learning, no downstream task validation
Poor evaluation metrics: Top-10 accuracy 51-89% on 1401 classes uninspiring, Macro-F1 < 0.1 on HSG-topology suggests task poorly defined or intractable

strengths: First large-scale spatial multigraph dataset addressing genuine gap in graph benchmarks; preserves rich geometric information typically collapsed into single edges
Exceptional scale (11.6M static + 5.1M dynamic graphs across 1401 classes) with diversity exceeding all existing graph classification datasets
High-quality engineering in Poly2Graph pipeline: 10^6× speedup and 20-40× memory efficiency over prior methods; well-integrated use of non-Bloch band theory, algebraic geometry, and image processing
Theoretical contribution showing spectral graphs as universal topological fingerprints for polynomials, vectors, and matrices via Toeplitz decomposition
Exemplary dataset release: open-source tools, permissive licenses, comprehensive documentation, multiple data formats, rich attributes preserving geometric structure
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, outstanding visualizations, extensive appendices with mathematical background and tutorials
Provides practical utility for two communities (graph learning and condensed matter physics); enables future research in geometry-aware learning and materials discovery
weaknesses: Benchmarking is incomplete and admittedly minimal: cannot evaluate on HSG-three-band (9.1M), HSG-12M (11.6M), or T-HSG-5M; only 5 epochs without early stopping; no comparison with multigraph-specific GNN methods despite existing work in literature

Component fragmentation is an intrinsic limitation particularly affecting high-band and long-range systems; current mitigation (node merging) is ad-hoc and impact on downstream learning not quantified
Limited analysis of why GNNs struggle beyond showing they do: no ablation studies on featurization, no systematic investigation of which geometric properties are learnable vs. intractable

Dataset design choices inadequately justified: sampling scheme (13×7)² per class chosen empirically; balanced sampling may not reflect natural distributions; HSG-topology achieves extreme imbalance (660.2×) that appears artificially difficult
Temporal dataset (T-HSG-5M) captures parameter sweeps not true temporal dynamics; claimed suitability for temporal tasks not validated; feels like incomplete extension
Theoretical contributions (Section 6, Appendix E) on universality feel tangential and underdeveloped; Toeplitz connection interesting but practical utility unclear
Limited demonstrated impact: motivated by materials science but no case studies; unclear where spectral graph dataset has enabled actual scientific discovery
No comparisons with spatial graph methods, multigraph-specific algorithms, or physics-based baselines; no comparison with OpenStreetMap despite noting it as most relevant resource

strengths: First large-scale spatial multigraph dataset (11.6M graphs, 1401 classes), addressing a genuine gap in graph learning benchmarks
High-performance Poly2Graph pipeline achieving ~10^5× speedup through clever algorithmic design (accelerated root-finding, adaptive resolution)
Strong mathematical grounding connecting non-Bloch band theory, algebraic geometry, and morphological image processing with rigorous exposition
Excellent reproducibility: open-source release (MIT/CC-BY licenses), comprehensive tutorials, detailed experimental configurations enabling full reproducibility
Thorough benchmarking with 8 GNN baselines, careful hyperparameter matching (within 4%), multiple seeds, and diverse metrics (Top-k, Macro-F1)
Multiple dataset variants (HSG-one/two/three-band, HSG-topology, T-HSG-5M) tailored to different research needs and computational budgets
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Poly2Graph primarily combines existing techniques (non-Bloch theory from Tai & Lee 2023, standard morphological image processing, accelerated eigensolvers); contribution is engineering rather than fundamental innovation
Component fragmentation is an acknowledged but unresolved limitation affecting data quality, particularly for multi-band and long-range hopping systems that are of greatest physics interest

Moderate benchmark results undermine utility claims: Top-1 accuracy on HSG-12M is only 0.546 (barely above random for 1401 classes), with large gaps to Top-10 accuracy (0.952) suggesting models assign plausible candidates but fail at precise classification

Reference featurization reduces rich curved edge geometry to 6 scalars; authors acknowledge discarding 'full continuous details,' yet do not validate richer alternatives despite GIN's collapse without edge features

Physics impact claims are unvalidated: no experiments demonstrate that ML predictions guide materials discovery, enable topological property prediction, or outperform domain knowledge; inverse design motivation is plausible but untested

Speculative universality claims (Section 5, Appendix F) lack experimental validation; connection between spectral graphs and general polynomials/matrices is interesting but underdeveloped without proof-of-concept applications
Missing comparisons to spatial graph CNNs (Danel et al. 2019) and multigraph-specific methods (Egressy et al. 2024); standard GNNs may not be appropriate baselines for spatial multigraphs

Insufficient pipeline validation: 'validation' through visual inspection of hundreds of examples is not quantitative; no ablation studies on Poly2Graph components; no comparison to finite-size diagonalization ground truth

strengths: Large-scale dataset with exceptional class diversity (11.6M graphs, 1401 classes) addressing underexplored spatial multigraph benchmarks
Technically sound physics-grounded contribution using non-Bloch band theory with legitimate scientific motivation
Open-source Poly2Graph pipeline achieving 10^5× speedup with comprehensive documentation and tutorials
Valid observation that existing benchmarks overwhelmingly ignore geometric information in spatial multigraphs
weaknesses: Very weak benchmark results (46% Top-1 accuracy on HSG-12M) with enormous Top-1/Top-10 gap (46% vs 95.2%), suggesting task may not effectively advance spatial multigraph learning research or reveal actionable insights

Limited technical novelty: Poly2Graph primarily engineers existing techniques (non-Bloch theory, image processing) without algorithmic innovations; component fragmentation limitation affects complex cases
Overstated claims of universality and broad applicability; spectral graphs' connection to general graph learning feels forced; practical utility of algebra-to-graph bridge underdeveloped

Synthetic dataset construction with only 2 free coefficients in fixed polynomial families lacks validation against real physical systems; characteristic polynomial class prediction is domain-specific with unclear scientific value

Incomplete evaluation: no ablations on edge feature designs (curvature, torsion, splines), minimal investigation of what causes poor performance, temporal dataset (T-HSG-5M) barely evaluated, no error analysis

Questionable spatial multigraph framing: reference featurization is simplistic and direction-ignorant, deliberately discarding geometric information the paper claims to preserve; underdeveloped exploration of richer encodings during benchmarking

Benchmark design issues: fixed training budget (100 epochs) may unfairly constrain more expressive models; hyperparameter equalization could introduce bias; limited baseline diversity (8 GNNs); GraphSAGE superiority attributed speculatively without ablation
Narrow domain applicability: non-Hermitian spectral graphs are highly specialized with tenuous connections to materials discovery; inverse design motivation is underdeveloped and unvalidated

strengths: First large-scale spatial multigraph benchmark addressing genuine gap in graph representation learning; 11.6M graphs across 1401 classes with exceptional diversity
Poly2Graph achieves ~10⁵× speedup via novel algorithmic choices (Frobenius companions, two-stage adaptive resolution, GPU acceleration) enabling systematic spectral graph research
Grounded in rigorous physics (non-Bloch band theory, Ronkin function) making dataset authentic rather than synthetic
Comprehensive benchmarking of 8 GNN architectures with careful hyperparameter matching and multiple evaluation metrics appropriate for high-class-diversity setting
Excellent reproducibility: open-source code, detailed tutorials, extensive appendices (48 pages), stratified data splits, multiple seeds
Clear technical findings: edge geometry substantially matters (GINE 46% vs GIN 6.3%), high Top-10 accuracy (95.2%) enables practical inverse-design workflows
Proposes spectral graphs as universal topological fingerprints connecting condensed-matter physics with graph learning in novel ways
Multiple dataset variants (one/two/three-band, static/temporal, balanced/imbalanced) enable progressive evaluation and diverse research directions
weaknesses: Representation gap: proposed 6-dimensional edge summaries discard continuous geometric information (curvature, torsion); raw coordinate sequences provided but integration with standard GNNs unclear
Component fragmentation in high-band/long-hopping systems: low density-of-states regions cause spurious disconnections; extent and prevalence across 1401 classes not quantified
Moderate Top-1 accuracy on full dataset (46-54%) with large Top-1 vs Top-10 gap (54.6% vs 95.2%) suggests task difficulty may limit practical deployment for inverse design
Limited algorithmic innovation: benchmarks existing methods without proposing spatial-multigraph-aware architectures; no mechanistic analysis of why GraphSAGE wins or ablation of edge features
Temporal component (T-HSG-5M) underexplored: 5.1M temporal graphs introduced but not benchmarked with temporal GNN baselines; claims about temporal dynamics lack evidence
Unclear practical applications beyond materials science despite 'universality' claims; Toeplitz decomposition universality is theoretically elegant but practical applications speculative
Incomplete evaluation of spatial geometry: no ablation studies isolating contribution of edge coordinates vs attributes; missing visualization of learned representations and per-class analysis
Class imbalance in HSG-topology variant (660:1 ratio) extreme; no mitigation strategies (class reweighting) discussed or evaluated
